title: Geometric restriction between topoi of internal group actions
statement:
Fix a universe and a small site $(C,J)$ with finite limits [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(C,J)$, and let $K,L$ be sheaves of groups with values in that universe. A $K$-object is a sheaf of sets $X$ together with a sheaf morphism $K\times X\to X$ satisfying the identity and associativity equations; morphisms are equivariant sheaf maps. Write $\mathscr E^K$ for this category. For the action site $C_K$ with arrows $(f,a):V\to U$, $a\in K(V)$, composition $(f,a)(g,b)=(fg,bg^*a)$ and topology generated by covers whose underlying base families cover [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], there is an equivalence $\mathscr E^K\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(C_K)$. It sends an action to the presheaf with restriction $x\mapsto a\cdot f^*x$. In particular $\mathscr E^K$ is a topos presented by a small site.

For every morphism of group sheaves $\theta:L\to K$, restriction of action $q_\theta^{-1}:\mathscr E^K\to\mathscr E^L$ has a right adjoint and preserves finite limits, so is the inverse image of a geometric morphism $q_\theta:\mathscr E^L\to\mathscr E^K$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. There is a geometric morphism $p_K:\mathscr E^K\to\mathscr E$ whose inverse image equips a sheaf with trivial action. The equality $q_\theta^{-1}p_K^{-1}=p_L^{-1}$ on sheaves and maps specifies a canonical geometric isomorphism $p_Kq_\theta\cong p_L$. Identity and successive restrictions carry their literal identity and composition identifications.

Let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $C$ and put $R_K=p_K^{-1}R$, $R_L=p_L^{-1}R$. On the ringed topoi $(\mathscr E^K,R_K)$ and $(\mathscr E^L,R_L)$, the module pullbacks along $p_K$ and $q_\theta$ are respectively trivial inflation and restriction of action, and are exact. Under the action-site equivalence their tensor comparisons send $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$ with the diagonal action and their unit comparisons are the identity on the regular ring. A ring-sheaf map $\varphi:R\to R'$ induces the same map on these trivially acted-on ring sheaves. The resulting squares with $p_K$ and $q_\theta$ commute as ringed-topos morphisms, with identity comparison on underlying sheaves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-internal-action-sheaf-equivalence] to $K$ (and to $L$). Its section-pinned equivalence has exactly the restriction $x\mapsto a\cdot f^*x$ required here, on the same small action site. Thus both action categories have small-site presentations and are topoi by [def-weil-pbc-topos].

proof.text: For $\theta:L\to K$, [lem-sfb-internal-action-coinduction] gives the sheaf-valued right adjoint $B_\theta$ to actual action restriction. Finite-limit preservation is [lem-sfb-internal-restriction-geometric-coherence]. Combining these two properties gives the geometric morphism $q_\theta$ by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Apply the same construction to $K\to1$: actions of $1$ are ordinary sheaves, so this supplies $p_K$ with trivial-inflation inverse image.

proof.text: The literal identifications in [lem-sfb-internal-restriction-geometric-coherence] give $q_\theta^{-1}p_K^{-1}=p_L^{-1}$, hence the specified geometric comparison $p_Kq_\theta\cong p_L$, together with identity and composition coherence. For a base ring $R$, give $R_K$ and $R_L$ the identity structural ring maps of that lemma. Its coefficient-square assertion applies to every $\varphi:R\to R'$ and fixes both composite structural maps and the underlying comparisons.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-internal-restriction-module-tensor] now hold: the inverse images are restriction and trivial inflation, and their structural ring maps are identities. Its multiplication identification of the module pullback gives precisely the stated module functors and their exactness. Its action-site tensor comparison gives the diagonal action and $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$, with identity on the regular unit. Its naturality and coherence, together with step 3, give all claimed ringed module comparisons.
